dedupe_keys.name: cwa space weather operational office products and taiwan geomagnetic disturbance index

description: The Space Weather Operational Office of the Central Weather Administration of Taiwan publishes space weather reports, warnings and products online. Its observation pages cover FORMOSAT radio occultation electron density profiles and ionospheric products, ionosonde and total electron content observations, solar images, sunspots, coronagraph, solar wind, X-ray flux, energetic particles and the geomagnetic field in Taiwan; its forecast pages cover HF radio absorption, the ionosphere and thermosphere, auroral visibility, the magnetopause position, scintillation and solar wind propagation. The Taiwan geomagnetic disturbance monitoring page shows the Taiwan disturbance index (TWDI), the median of disturbance values from three-component magnetometer stations of the CWA Seismological Center after a quiet-time reference is removed, plotted like the global Dst index from -500 to 100 nT for the current month or the past 7, 15 or 30 days. The data download page points to the CWA open data platform, the Taiwan earthquake and geophysical data system, the Taiwan Analysis Center for FORMOSAT occultation data and other archives, and invites email requests. Access to the pages is free; the site states that CWA holds copyright and that reuse needs authorisation, so no open licence covers the pages themselves. Caveats: the pages are mainly in Chinese, and a notice says recent disturbance data are not yet calibrated because of station maintenance. Coverage is Taiwan, with global solar and ionospheric context. It supports hazard exposure analysis of space weather for power grids, GNSS and HF communications; related records are the NICT space weather forecast and the BRIN SWIFtS service.
